unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U27: Distinguish electronic recognition,contract formation and reliable retention

payload.title: Electronic form is only one part of legal validity
payload.core_explanation_md:
The IT Act supplies the described recognition of electronic records and signatures and supports electronic contracting and government services. A record is not invalid solely because it is electronic, but that does not prove capacity, consent, authority or every other contract requirement. Distinguish the originator, the intended addressee and an intermediary carrying or storing the message.

Retention requires the described accessibility, accurate representation and origin/destination/time details, subject to the statutory qualification for automatically generated transmission information. A screenshot may preserve appearance while losing relevant metadata or the reliable original record. Design the evidence trail so the record can be retrieved and its integrity assessed later; a file existing somewhere is not enough.

self_check.prompt_text: Does electronic recognition itself prove the sender had authority?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Form, authority and the other validity requirements differ.

payload.stem_md: A bank retains a record in a proprietary format it can no longer open. Which retention feature is missing?

options.explanation_md: That does not restore electronic accessibility.
That does not make the record usable.
Retention requires usable access, not mere storage.
A display preference does not establish that the retained record remains accessible for later reference.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Retention requires usable access, not mere storage.

payload.stem_md: A message passes through a hosting provider to its intended recipient. Why distinguish the host from the originator and addressee?

options.text_md: The statutory roles have different meanings and consequences
options.explanation_md: Carrying a record does not automatically make the host its creator or intended recipient.

options.text_md: Every host necessarily signs every message
The recipient always becomes the originator
options.explanation_md: The intended recipient and the person generating or sending the record have distinct defined roles.

options.text_md: Electronic messages have no legally relevant parties

payload.correct_explanation_md: Carrying a record does not automatically make the host its creator or intended recipient.
